newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 14.

text.p: Parliament's privileges committee will begin a hearing early next week into an alleged assault against National MP John Banks by Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters. Speaker Doug Kidd had referred a complaint against Peters by Alliance leader Jim Anderton to the committee. Attorney-General Paul East, who was elected chairman of the committee, said it would meet early next week. Page 1.

The government is likely to join the Fish and Game Council in appealing against a court ruling that allows Maoris to fish for trout without a licence in their tribal areas. The council said on Thursday it would appeal against Wanganui judge Andrew Decroft's decision. It will be represented by Sir Geoffrey Palmer, a former prime minister. Page 1.

The government would introduce a law banning the cloning of humans, Justice Minister Doug Graham said on Thursday. Labour list MP Dianne Yates has already introduced a private member's bill -- the Human Assistance and Reproduction Technology Bill -- that proposes a ban on cloning. However, Graham said Yate's bill did not reflect government policy and went far beyond recommendations of the National Ethics Committee. Page 2.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger made it clear on Thursday there was no future for universal taxpayer-funded superannuation once the surcharge was removed. His strong statement in Parliament is being taken as a sign that the current superannuation scheme is at an end as the government prepares to carry out a Coalition promise to remove the surcharge and hold a referendum on compulsory superannuation. Page 2.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Treasurer Winston Peters may lay a complaint with the police after a radio station said it received a call purporting to be from a parliamentary security guard about Peters's drinking. Bolger's chief press secretary, Richard Griffin, said on Thursday night that legal advice would also be taken during the next day or two over possible litigation action. Page 2.

A secret Inland Revenue Department report showed that deferring the tax cuts from this year till July next year would cost the community $2.9 billion, ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble said on Thursday. Prebble told the Wellington Regional Chamber of Commerce that the department had brought leading tax expert Gerald Scully to New Zealand to study the dead weight of taxation. Page 2.

Serious Fraud Office director Charles Sturt had no role in the investigation of Aotearoa Television Network, Attorney-General Paul East told Parliament on Thursday. The SFO began the inquiry into ATN after disclosures that NZ First MP Tuku Morgan had spent money on expensive clothes after he resigned as a director. Page 2.

Homeowners and businesses could see a small cut in floating interest rates soon and there was some relief for exporters from the high New Zealand dollar after Thursday's Reserve Bank projections. While some economists tipped a fall in variable lending rates soon, others said it was unlikely. Central bank governor Don Brash's latest view of the economy, out on Thursday, brought down short term wholsale interest rates by 20 points to 7.38 percent and knocked more than half a United States cent off the value of the Kiwi dollar, to just under US70 cents, giving a little relief to exportes. Page 9.

Fletcher Challenge Energy has boosted its stake in the offshore Kupe gas field by 34.25 percent but voting fights on the new stake have been frozen till the Commerce Commission investigates dominance and competition concerns. Fletcher increased its stake from 2.5 percent to 36.75 percent through a deal that saw it buy Norcen Energy's 20 percent stake in Kupe and Western Mining Corporation (NZ) Ltd's 40 percent interest. It then sold ECNZ 25.75 percent. Page 9.

Computer hardware and software distributor Triumph Industries was not paying a final dividend after a $6.64 million bottom-line loss because of one-off costs on its 1996 year result, it said on Thursday. Triumph produced a pre-tax trading surplus of $2.06 million for the year till December 31 from total revenue of $113.75 million, which was up 15 percent on the previous period on an annualised basis. Page 9.

Sky Television announced a $250 million seven-year loan facility on Thursday to fund its expansion, including its new satellite broadcasting service. Sky chief financial officer Paul Smart said the loan was the most signficant undertaken by the pay television network. The loan covered refinancing existing debt, as well as the satellite expansion and capital expenses involved in increasing subscriber numbers, Smart said. Page 9.

Some share analysts have criticised Brierley Investments for the confusion that led some to overstate BIL's net tangible asset backing by seven cents a share. Some had to reassess the treatment of Nova Trust's $208 million investment in Coles Myer. Nova Trust was formed to hold the stake in Coles Myer, funding half the total purchase with the balance held by ACIL. But BIL denied any wrongdoing on Thursday and said the figures were there for all to see. Page 9.

Wilson and Horton associate Radio Network is on the acquisition trial again, securing conditional contracts to buy two Christchurch radio stations. Radio Network, which acquired Radio New Zealand's 41 commercial stations and 12 stations operated by Prospect Radio last year, already has three stations in Christchurch. The proposed acquisition of stations C93 and i94FM, both owned by Ian Harris and Roger Crozier, is still being subject to the Commerce Commission approval. Page 9.
